column1: # mapping_set_title: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 to NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile) Schema Mappings

# mapping_set_description: Schema-level mappings between the ISO/IEC 22989:2022 (Artificial intelligence concepts and terminology) and NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile, an AI RMF cross-sectoral profile) LinkML schemas. Mappings align lifecycle, actor and risk-category constructs, with several narrow matches reflecting NIST's generative-AI-specific risk taxonomy.

column10: comment
NIST GenAI risk is a specialisation of the ISO/IEC 22989 risk item targeted at generative AI.
Both enumerations partition the AI lifecycle into stages; NIST GenAI uses a coarser 5-stage scheme.
Both refer to the early design phase of the AI lifecycle.
Both refer to model development activities.
Same lifecycle stage.
Same lifecycle stage; ISO/IEC 22989 label additionally calls out monitoring.
Same end-of-life lifecycle stage.
Both enumerate roles or tasks performed by actors involved in AI systems.
Both refer to end users of an AI system.
ISO/IEC 22989 AI subject corresponds to NIST's affected-individuals-and-communities actor.
ISO/IEC 22989 AI partner roles overlap with NIST third-party entities providing supporting services.
ISO/IEC 22989 relevant authority aligns with NIST's governance-and-oversight actor role.
ISO/IEC 22989 AI auditor performs test, evaluation, verification and validation similar to NIST's TEVV actor.
ISO/IEC 22989 bias categories are subtypes of NIST's harmful-bias-or-homogenization GenAI risk.
Privacy property addresses the data-privacy GenAI risk category.
Security property addresses the information-security GenAI risk category.
Integrity property addresses the information-integrity GenAI risk category.
Several GenAI risk categories (ecosystem, environmental, cultural) are realised as ISO/IEC 22989 societal-impact categories.
Human-machine teaming structures address the human-AI-configuration GenAI risk category.
NIST suggested actions populate AI lifecycle processes addressing GenAI risks.
